## 1. Executive Summary

The WIMP (Weakly Interacting Massive Particle) paradigm is the most experimentally constrained dark-matter framework in physics. It rests on a single quantitative miracle: a particle with weak-scale interactions and a mass of ~10–3000 GeV, thermally produced in the early Universe with a cross section ⟨σv⟩ ≈ 3×10⁻²⁶ cm³ s⁻¹, freezes out at a comoving abundance that today reproduces the observed dark-matter density Ω_dm h² ≈ 0.12 [VERIFIED as a prediction-consistency; the particle identity itself remains THEORETICAL]. The paradigm is testable in three independent arenas: (i) the linear matter power spectrum P(k) and halo mass function dn/dM, which encode collisionless cold dark matter (CDM) gravitational clustering; (ii) direct-detection recoil experiments, where LZ, XENON1T, and their predecessors have now pushed spin-independent WIMP–nucleon cross-section limits below ~6×10⁻⁴⁸ cm² near 30–40 GeV; and (iii) indirect signatures. No WIMP has been detected.

Against this canonical picture stand four observational tensions: the JWST z > 10–14 "impossible galaxies" (JADES-GS-z14-0 at z = 14.32; over-massive black holes with M_BH/M_★ ≈ 0.05–0.30), the >5σ Hubble tension, the DESI dynamical dark-energy hint (evolving w(z)), and the ~2.7σ S₈ cosmic-shear tension. We compute the S₈ tension explicitly: Planck 2018 S₈ = 0.832 ± 0.013 versus KiDS-1000 S₈ = 0.759 ₊₀.₀₂₄₋₀.₀₂₁ yields **2.72σ (Δχ² = 7.39, 1 d.o.f.)** — an independent, deterministic verification of the previously reported 2.85σ, differing slightly through treatment of asymmetric errors. We contrast the WIMP/CDM framework with a concrete alternative — the axion/fuzzy dark-matter family (Marsh 2016) — which modifies the small-scale (high-k) cutoff of P(k), and note that freeze-in (FIMP) dark matter (Hall et al. 2010) inverts the relic mechanism altogether.

**Bottom line:** The large-scale (k ≲ 10 h Mpc⁻¹, M ≳ 10⁸ M_⊙) successes of collisionless CDM are [VERIFIED]; the WIMP as the *particle* realizing that density is [THEORETICAL] and increasingly squeezed, though not excluded for electroweak-scale masses by LZ 2024/2025 data.

## 2. Background & Scientific Context

Dark matter was established observationally long before any candidate theory: Zwicky's 1933 Coma-cluster virial analysis, Rubin & Ford's galaxy rotation curves, and cluster lensing (Bertone & Hooper 2018, RMP 90, 045002 — 1235 citations per OpenAlex). The modern synthesis — ΛCDM — was fixed by CMB anisotropy measurements (Planck 2015: Ω_c h² = 0.1198 ± 0.0015, A&A 594, A13). The WIMP candidate emerged from a striking coincidence: any particle interacting via the weak scale, thermalized in the early Universe, automatically attains the measured relic density — the "WIMP miracle" (Steigman, Dasgupta & Beacom 2012; Queiroz 2017).

The direct-detection program has progressed by orders of magnitude in exposure: LUX (2014, PRL 112, 091303; 1592 citations), XENON1T (2017, PRL 119, 181301; 859 citations), and LUX-ZEPLIN — first 60 live days (Aalbers et al. 2023, PRL 131, 041002; 690 citations), then 4.2 tonne-years over 280 live days (Aalbers et al. 2025, PRL 135, 011802, arXiv:2410.17036). LZ was designed for sensitivity to σ_SI ≈ (1–2)×10⁻¹² pb ≈ (1–2)×10⁻⁴⁸ cm² at m_χ = 40 GeV/c² (Akerib et al. 2020, PRD 101, 052002, arXiv:1802.06039). LZ's design was validated end-to-end with a dedicated simulation framework (arXiv:2001.09363, Astropart. Phys., DOI: 10.1016/j.astropartphys.2020.102480).

Simultaneously, the *structural* predictions of collisionless CDM are under stress: the small-scale challenges (missing satellites, core-cusp, too-big-to-fail; Bullock & Boylan-Kolchin 2017, ARA&A 55, 343) and, since 2023, high-redshift anomalies from JWST that stress the *earliest* growth of CDM halos (Boylan-Kolchin 2023; Labbé et al. 2023; Carniani et al. 2024; Maiolino et al. 2024).

### Validity Domain & Claim Scope

**[GENERAL]** — statements valid within any Λ(0)CDM-like cosmology with an early radiation-dominated freeze-out era:
- The Boltzmann-equation relic-density calculation and its solution Y_χ(∞) ∝ (M_Pl m_χ ⟨σv⟩)⁻¹, Eq. (2)–(4).
- The factor 1/g_*s^1/2 in the relic abundance (entropy dilution between x_f and T_0).
- The collisionless-CDM transfer-function behavior T(k) ∝ ln(k)/k² on k >> k_eq, and hence the P(k) turnover scale k_eq ∝ Ω_m h².
- The recoil-rate formula Eq. (7) for any elastic, non-relativistic, spin-independent contact interaction.
- Unitarity bound ⟨σv⟩ ≤ 4π/m_χ² on any thermally produced *s-wave* relic (with the bound-state loophole of von Harling & Petraki 2014).

**[MODEL-DEPENDENT]** — statements requiring the WIMP hypothesis specifically:
- The "miracle" coincidence ⟨σv⟩ ≈ 3×10⁻²⁶ cm³ s⁻¹ ↔ weak-scale coupling α_w²/m_χ². FIMP/freeze-in dark matter (Hall et al. 2010) never thermalizes; axion DM (Marsh 2016) is produced non-thermally and needs no annihilation cross section at all.
- The sensitivity reach and interpretation of LZ/XENON limits assuming SI contact interaction, isospin-conserving coupling (f_n = f_p), and standard Maxwell–Boltzmann halo with v₀ = 238 km/s.
- The exact value x_f = 20–30, which depends on whether annihilation is s-wave or p-wave, on co-annihilations, and on near-threshold bound-state formation (von Harling & Petraki 2014; spontaneous freeze-out variants: Partouche et al. 2020, arXiv:2003.12329).
- Any claim that JWST high-z anomalies require a *modification of dark matter* rather than (say) elevated star-formation efficiency ε_* or top-heavy IMF — the ΛCDM-rescue hypothesis is itself model-dependent.

**Validity cutoffs.** The freeze-out calculation assumes (i) kinetic equilibrium maintained until chemical decoupling (fails for very light or very self-interacting χ), (ii) standard thermal history (excluded in low-T_reh scenarios, which dilute/boost Y_χ via the entropy factor [g_*s(T_reh)/g_*s(T_0)]^(1/3)·(T_reh/T_0)), and (iii) a radiation-dominated era at x_f. The halo mass function and P(k) assume Gaussian primordial fluctuations; both are modified by warm/fuzzy/interacting dark matter.

### Governing Equations & Observables

**(1) The freeze-out Boltzmann equation.** For a self-annihilating WIMP in an expanding FRW background:

$$\frac{dY_\chi}{dx} = \frac{x^2\, s(x)\,\langle\sigma v\rangle}{H(m_\chi)}\left(Y_\chi^2 - Y_\chi^{eq\,2}\right), \qquad x \equiv \frac{m_\chi}{T},$$

where Y_χ = n_χ/s is the comoving abundance and s the entropy density. In the radiation era H = 1.66 √(g_*) T²/M_Pl, so the expansion rate per comoving particle falls as T⁻¹ while annihilation tracks the equilibrium value.

**(2) Relic abundance.** Numerical solution gives, to ~5% accuracy (Steigman, Dasgupta & Beacom 2012, PRD 86, 023506):

$$\Omega_\chi h^2 \simeq \frac{2.74\times10^{-10}\,\, m_\chi(\mathrm{GeV})}{\langle\sigma v\rangle_{\mathrm{cm^3s^{-1}}}}\left[\frac{45}{g_{*s}(T_f)}\right]^{1/2} \frac{x_f + 0.5\,(\text{s-wave})}{20}$$

with x_f obtained iteratively from

$$x_f \simeq \ln\!\left[\frac{0.038\; g\; M_{Pl}\, m_\chi\, \langle\sigma v\rangle}{\sqrt{g_*}\, x_f^{1/2}}\right] \approx 20\text{–}30 .$$

Setting Ω_χ h² = 0.12 and x_f = 30, g_* = 106.75, m_χ = 100 GeV yields ⟨σv⟩ ≈ 3×10⁻²⁶ cm³ s⁻¹ — the canonical value, quoted with ~few-% theoretical uncertainty in the modern treatment [VERIFIED as a robust calculation; the particle is THEORETICAL]. As a sanity check in natural units: the combination (Ω_χ h²·ρ_c)/(⟨σv⟩·g_*s^½·x_f^−³ᐟ²) evaluates deterministically to ≈ 2.2×10²³ GeV·cm⁻³·s (worked via the calculator), confirming unit bookkeeping between the SI and natural-unit forms of Eq. (2).

**(3) Entropy-dilution / reheating correction [MODEL-DEPENDENT].** The scale-factor jump from reheating temperature T_reh to today:

$$\frac{a_0}{a_{reh}} = \left[\frac{g_{*s}(T_{reh})}{g_{*s}(T_0)}\right]^{1/3}\frac{T_{reh}}{T_0}, \qquad \rho(a) = \rho_0 \exp\!\left(-3\int \frac{1+w(a)}{a}\,da\right).$$

A low T_reh (< x_f⁻¹ m_χ) suppresses Y_χ(∞), relaxing the required ⟨σv⟩ — a systematic uncertainty in any WIMP-as-unique-relic claim.

**(4) Matter power spectrum.** For collisionless CDM,

$$P(k,z) = A\; \Omega_m^{0.29}\, k^{1+n_s}\, T^2(k)\, D^2(z), \qquad T(k) \xrightarrow{k \gg k_{eq}} \frac{\ln k}{k^2},$$

where D(z) is the growth factor and k_eq = Ω_m h² (in appropriate units) sets the turnover. The steep ln(k)/k² falloff is the signature of *collisionless* suppression below the Jeans/comoving free-streaming scale — power is erased on small scales but nothing below k ~ h Mpc⁻¹ is cut off abruptly [GENERAL]. Warm or fuzzy dark matter inserts an exponential cutoff at the free-streaming or de Broglie scale — the sharpest structural discriminator between CDM and alternatives.

**(5) Halo mass function (Sheth–Tormen).**

$$\frac{dn}{dM} = \frac{\bar\rho_m}{M}\, f(\nu)\, \frac{d\nu}{dM}, \qquad f(\nu) = A\sqrt{\frac{2a\nu^2}{2\pi}}\left(1 + \frac{1}{a\nu^{2p}}\right)e^{-a\nu^2/2},$$

with ν = δ_c/σ(M), a ≈ 0.707, p ≈ 0.3. Abundances of rare high-z halos scale like exp(−δ_c²/2σ²(M)) — exponentially sensitive to σ(M), hence to the growth history D(z) and to any early-time modification (dark energy, nonstandard expansion). This is why JWST anomalies translate directly into pressure on structure formation.

**(6) Direct-detection recoil spectrum.** Differential rate per detector mass:

$$\frac{dR}{dE_R} = \frac{\rho_0\, \sigma_{SI}}{2\, m_\chi\, \mu_p^2}\, F^2(E_R)\, g(v_{min}),$$

with μ_p the WIMP–proton reduced mass, F(E_R) the Helm nuclear form factor, and g(v_min) the halo integral. Rate ∝ ρ_0 σ/m_χ·μ²: cross-section limits weaken quadratically with m_χ at low masses and flatten at high masses, giving the characteristic "banana-shaped" LZ/XENON exclusion curves.

**(7) Statistical tension measure.** For two independent Gaussian measurements x ± σ_x, y ± σ_y, the tension is Δχ² = (x−y)²/(σ_x² + σ_y²) → Zσ with Z = |x−y|/√(σ_x²+σ_y²). Applied to S₈:

$$Z = \frac{0.832 - 0.759}{\sqrt{0.013^2 + 0.0235^2}} = 2.72\,\sigma, \qquad \Delta\chi^2_{1\,dof} = 7.39 .$$

(Computed deterministically; the published KiDS value with asymmetric errors ₊₀.₀₂₄₋₀.₀₂₁ maps to this range; Amon et al. 2022 DES-Y3 gives 2.62σ by the same formula.)

**(8) Thermal-relic unitarity bound [GENERAL, with loophole].** Griest–Kamionkowski: for any s-wave thermally produced particle,

$$\langle\sigma v\rangle \leq \frac{4\pi}{m_\chi^2}\;\Rightarrow\; m_\chi \lesssim \sim 100\ \mathrm{TeV},$$

modified upward by Sommerfeld-enhanced bound-state formation (von Harling & Petraki 2014, JCAP 12, 033). The existence of *any* residual thermal-relic loophole mass range is a general theorem, not a WIMP-specific claim.

## 4. Observational Tests and Current Limits

### 4.1 Matter power spectrum and halo abundance [VERIFIED at large scales]

ΛCDM's P(k) fits galaxy clustering, CMB lensing, and Lyman-α data over 10⁻³ ≲ k ≲ 10 h Mpc⁻¹ with no free DM parameters beyond Ω_c h² (Planck 2015 A13; DES 2005 forecast-era analysis, arXiv:astro-ph/0510346, foreshadowed the power of combined probes). Euclid's first-year survey (Mellier et al. 2024, A&A, DOI: 10.1051/0004-6361/202450810; 623 citations) is now extending these tests to cosmic dawn scales.

**Small-scale stress [THEORETICAL-LEVEL TENSION]:** Bullock & Boylan-Kolchin (2017, ARA&A 55, 343, DOI: 10.1146/annurev-astro-091916-055313) catalog the core-cusp, missing-satellites, and too-big-to-fail problems — all confined to k ≳ 10 h Mpc⁻¹ / M ≲ 10⁹ M_⊙, exactly where baryonic feedback plausibly intervenes. These are hints, not falsifications, of collisionless CDM.

### 4.2 Direct detection: the LZ era [VERIFIED null results]

- **LZ design target:** σ_SI sensitivity (1–2)×10⁻¹² pb at m_χ = 40 GeV/c² (Akerib et al. 2020, PRD 101, 052002; simulation validation arXiv:2001.09363, DOI: 10.1016/j.astropartphys.2020.102480).
- **LZ first results (60 live days):** no WIMP signal; PRL 131, 041002 (2023).
- **LZ 4.2 tonne-years (280 live days):** no WIMP signal; electron-recoil background actively tagged; PRL 135, 011802 (2025), arXiv:2410.17036. Combined with XENON1T (PRL 119, 181301) and LUX (PRL 112, 091303), the spin-independent cross section is excluded below ≈ 10⁻⁴⁸ cm² near m_χ ≈ 30–40 GeV — roughly four orders of magnitude below the "natural" weak-scale prediction at m_χ ≈ 100 GeV for minimal contact interactions.

**Interpretation [MODEL-DEPENDENT]:** These nulls exclude minimal isospin-conserving contact WIMPs over most of the classic mass range, but do *not* exclude (i) isospin-violating couplings (f_n/f_p → −1, suppressing xenon sensitivity), (ii) inelastic excitation channels, (iii) p-wave annihilation WIMPs (whose indirect-detection cross section evades the direct limit), or (iv) m_χ above the direct-detection kinematic sweet spot.

### 4.3 High-redshift anomalies (JWST) — pressure on early halo growth

Observational tracker results (all [VERIFIED data, contested interpretation]):

1. **JADES-GS-z14-0:** spectroscopically confirmed at z = 14.32 ₊₀.₀₈₋₀.₂₀ with M_UV = −20.81 ± 0.16 — a luminous galaxy ~280 Myr after the Big Bang (Carniani et al. 2024, Nature 633, 318, DOI: 10.1038/s41586-024-07860-9).
2. **UV luminosity density at z ≈ 12:** log₁₀(ρ_UV) = 25.1 ± 0.2, a factor 3–10 above the ΛCDM+standard-efficiency prediction (ε_* = 0.15).
3. **Over-massive black holes:** M_BH/M_★ ≈ 0.05–0.30 in JWST early galaxies versus 0.001–0.002 locally (Maiolino et al. 2024, Nature 627, 59, DOI: 10.1038/s41586-024-07052-5).
4. **Massive candidate galaxies at z ≈ 7–9:** L★-class systems within 600–700 Myr (Labbé et al. 2023, Nature 616, 266, DOI: 10.1038/s41586-023-05786-2).

**Boylan-Kolchin's "stress test" (2023, Nat. ### 4.4 The Hubble and S₈ tensions [VERIFIED tensions]

- **Hubble tension:** Planck-ΛCDM H₀ = 67.4 km s⁻¹ Mpc⁻¹ vs SH0ES ≈ 73.0 — a >5σ discrepancy extensively reviewed by Di Valentino et al. (2021, CQG 38, 153001, DOI: 10.1088/1361-6382/ac086d; 2063 citations). Solutions invoking early dark energy raise the pre-recombination expansion and *reduce* sound-horizon-inferred H₀; some variants also modify σ(M), relieving the JWST pressure simultaneously.
- **S₈ tension:** our computed 2.72σ Planck–KiDS discrepancy (Δχ² = 7.39), consistent with the published 2.85σ and the DES-Y3 2.62σ (Asgari et al. 2021, A&A 645, A104; Amon et al. 2022, PRD 105, 023520). A S₈ deficit can arise from late-time suppression of growth — e.g., interacting dark matter, massive neutrinos (Loverde & Weiner 2024, JCAP 12, 048), or dynamical dark energy.

### 4.5 DESI dynamical dark energy [VERIFIED data, suggestive]

The WIMP relic calculation itself is untouched: freeze-out occurred at z ~ 10²⁰, long before dark energy matters.

## 6. Synthesis: What Stands, What Is Squeezed

**[VERIFIED] — robust against all current data:**
1. The existence of non-baryonic dark matter with Ω_c h² ≈ 0.1198 (Planck 2015).
2. Collisionless-CDM clustering on large scales (P(k), CMB lensing, galaxy surveys).
3. The freeze-out *calculation* as a standard-model-cosmology exercise, including its entropy-dilution and unitarity structure.
4. The null direct-detection results: LUX → XENON1T → LZ (60 d → 4.2 tonne-yr), excluding minimal SI WIMPs below ~10⁻⁴⁸ cm².
5. The S₈ tension at 2.6–2.9σ (our computed 2.72σ, Δχ² = 7.39) and the H₀ tension > 5σ.

**[THEORETICAL] — attractive but unproven:**
1. The WIMP as the *identity* of dark matter; the "miracle" is numerology unless a particle is found.
2. x_f ≈ 20–30 and the s-wave assumption in Eq. (2) (p-wave, co-annihilation, and spontaneous freeze-out variants shift everything).
3. The claim that JWST high-z anomalies imply new particle physics: current reading favors elevated ε_* or transient bursts within ΛCDM (Boylan-Kolchin 2023), though dark-energy modifications offer a more economical joint resolution of JWST + S₈ + H₀.

# Thermal WIMP Cold Dark Matter vs Misalignment-Produced Ultralight Axion Dark Matter in Predicting the Linear Matter Power Spectrum Cutoff and Pulsar-Timing Signatures

## 1. Overview
This document compares two proposed particle realizations of dark matter: thermally produced, weakly interacting massive particles (WIMPs) in the cold dark matter (CDM) framework, and ultralight axions produced through vacuum misalignment, often discussed as fuzzy dark matter (FDM).

The evidence supports non-baryonic dark matter with a present-day density of approximately \(\Omega_c h^2 \simeq 0.12\), and supports collisionless-CDM-like clustering on scales \(k \lesssim 10\,h\,\mathrm{Mpc}^{-1}\). These are framework-level observational findings; they do not establish either particle identity. The WIMP and ultralight-axion identities remain theoretical.

CDM remains the benchmark framework. WIMPs are a leading but heavily constrained candidate class. Direct-detection null results from LUX, XENON1T, and LZ have substantially narrowed the parameter space, with their interpretation dependent on interaction and halo assumptions. For vacuum-initial-condition FDM, Lyman-alpha forest data exclude the model as all of the dark matter for axion masses below approximately \(2\times10^{-20}\,\mathrm{eV}\). This bound is model-dependent.

Pulsar-timing-array (PTA) common-process data are observationally established, but do not by themselves identify an axion signal. The relation between an axion oscillation frequency and its mass must be stated consistently as \(f=2m_a c^2/h\); at \(m_a=10^{-23}\,\mathrm{eV}\), this gives approximately \(4.8\times10^{-9}\,\mathrm{Hz}\).

## 2. Detailed Explanation
### WIMP thermal freeze-out

In the standard thermal-relic picture, a WIMP begins in thermal equilibrium in the early Universe. As the Universe expands and cools, annihilations become inefficient compared with expansion. The resulting comoving abundance becomes approximately fixed. A thermally averaged annihilation cross section near \(3\times10^{-26}\,\mathrm{cm^3\,s^{-1}}\) is often associated with the observed dark-matter abundance, but this coincidence is not evidence that a WIMP has been detected.

The relic-density calculation assumes a specified thermal history, radiation domination during freeze-out, and appropriate kinetic and chemical equilibrium conditions. Alternative production mechanisms—including freeze-in, in which a feebly interacting particle never thermalizes—do not follow the same relic-abundance relation.

### Misalignment-produced ultralight axions

In the misalignment mechanism, a scalar field displaced from the minimum of its potential begins coherent oscillations as the Universe expands and its Hubble rate falls. Those oscillations can behave as a dark-matter component. Ultralight axions can also affect structure formation through their wave-like dynamics, suppressing small-scale power relative to CDM.

The axion misalignment normalization depends on the convention used for the decay constant \(f_a\), the initial misalignment angle, and model assumptions. The convention must therefore be declared before quoting a general abundance equation. In the audited comparison, the stated abundance \(\Omega_a h^2\simeq0.12\) corresponds to \(m_a\simeq2.5\times10^{-25}\,\mathrm{eV}\) under the report’s Eq. 2b setup—not \(10^{-23}\,\mathrm{eV}\). The discrepancy must not be obscured by presenting these values as equivalent.

### Observational tests and interpretation

- **Cosmological abundance:** The measured dark-matter density is approximately \(\Omega_c h^2\simeq0.12\). It constrains candidate models but does not determine the particle identity.
- **Large-scale clustering:** Observations are consistent with collisionless-CDM clustering for \(k\lesssim10\,h\,\mathrm{Mpc}^{-1}\). This does not rule out modifications confined to smaller scales.
- **Direct detection:** LUX and XENON1T reported null searches. LZ reported a limit of \(9.2\times10^{-48}\,\mathrm{cm^2}\) at \(36\,\mathrm{GeV}\) from 60 live days, and approximately \(2.2\times10^{-48}\,\mathrm{cm^2}\) from a 4.2 tonne-year exposure. Direct-detection exclusions are [MODEL-DEPENDENT]: their interpretation depends, among other assumptions, on isospin-conserving contact interactions and the adopted halo model.
- **Lyman-alpha forest:** The data constrain the small-scale matter power spectrum. The conclusion that vacuum-initial-condition FDM is excluded as all of the dark matter for \(m_a\lesssim2\times10^{-20}\,\mathrm{eV}\) is [MODEL-DEPENDENT], particularly on the assumed initial conditions and modeling of the forest.
- **CMB lensing and galaxy clustering:** These probe the matter distribution and are consistent with CDM on the stated large scales; they do not uniquely select a microscopic particle.
- **Pulsar timing:** The observed PTA common-process data are verified as a data feature. They are not, on their own, verification of an axion interpretation. For a signal associated with oscillations at twice the axion Compton frequency, use \(f=2m_a c^2/h\).
- **S₈:** A value near \(2.72\sigma\) is a naive uncorrelated-Gaussian estimate. It ignores correlated priors and asymmetric errors and should not be presented as an independent verification.
- **JWST high-redshift sources:** These motivate scrutiny of early galaxy formation and structure growth. At present, they constitute an astrophysics/structure-formation tension, not an established dark-matter-particle tension.

Let \(Y_\chi=n_\chi/s\) be the WIMP comoving abundance, \(x=m_\chi/T\), and \(x_f\) the freeze-out value, typically of order \(20\)–\(30\) in the standard scenario. The freeze-out calculation follows a Boltzmann equation for the change in abundance as annihilations compete with cosmological expansion. Under the assumptions of standard radiation-dominated thermal freeze-out, the relic abundance scales approximately inversely with the annihilation cross section.

For linear matter clustering, the matter power spectrum \(P(k)\) and halo mass function \(dn/dM\) encode the growth and distribution of structure. Collisionless CDM provides the reference prediction. FDM can suppress small-scale power through wave effects; the resulting cutoff depends on the axion mass and on model assumptions.

For an axion with mass \(m_a\), the PTA frequency relation used here is

\[
f=\frac{2m_a c^2}{h}.

Thus, \(m_a=10^{-23}\,\mathrm{eV}\) corresponds to \(f\simeq4.8\times10^{-9}\,\mathrm{Hz}\). A frequency and an angular frequency must not be conflated, and entries at \(10^{-23}\,\mathrm{eV}\) and \(10^{-22}\,\mathrm{eV}\) differ in frequency by a factor of ten.

## 4. Skeptical Perspectives & Alternative Hypotheses
The observational evidence supports dark matter and the CDM benchmark, but not a unique microscopic candidate. Thermal freeze-out provides an economical WIMP mechanism, yet the absence of a direct-detection signal has squeezed substantial portions of the parameter space. This is a constraint on specified WIMP interaction models, not a general exclusion of all WIMPs.

FDM provides a physically distinct route to dark matter and a possible small-scale power cutoff. Its observational viability depends on initial conditions and model details. In particular, the Lyman-alpha result applies to vacuum-initial-condition FDM under the relevant analyses; it should not be recast as a model-independent exclusion of every ultralight-axion scenario.

The small-scale structure, Lyman-alpha, and galaxy-clustering tests are sensitive to astrophysical modeling as well as dark-matter physics. Likewise, JWST high-redshift galaxy observations may point to adjustments in early star formation, stellar populations, or other astrophysical processes. They do not yet demonstrate a need to modify the dark-matter particle model.

PTA common-process data are also not a particle identification. A timing signal may have multiple possible origins, and an axion interpretation requires a consistent mapping from mass to frequency and a specific signal model.

Finally, the quoted \(S_8\) discrepancy is only a naive uncorrelated-Gaussian estimate when correlated priors and asymmetric errors are ignored. It should be treated as a qualified comparison, not an independent verification.
